newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Macao reports better than expected January cargo.
newsitem.headline: Macao reports better than expected January cargo.

text.p: Cargo throughput at Macao International airport during January was "much better than expected" totalling 2,396 tonnes, according to Michael Hanley, general manager of cargo handlers MASC Ogden Aviation Services.

The total compares with 3,831 tonnes during December and 4,417 in November, the highest cargo tonnage recorded since flights began into Macao in November 1995. Last January just 162 tonnes of cargo passed through the Portuguese enclave's new airport.
Hanley said the January total was made up of 51.5 per cent inbound, 33.5 percent outbound and 15 percent transhipments.

"It was better than we anticipated. After a quiet start it really picked up towards the end of the month as shippers tried to get goods out before Chinese New Year. Early February also saw a rush then it died," Hanley told Reuters in an interview.
Total cargo throughput at Macao is expected to increase by more than 60 percent this year to more than 33,000 tonnes compared with 25,000 tonnes in 1996, airport officials have forecast.

The MASC Ogden Cargo Centre is a joint venture between China's Macao Aviation Services Company and Ogden Aviation Services of the U.S. to provide cargo ground handling and aircraft maintenance. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
